# shapvalues

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

`shapvalues` computes Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) for the predictions
of any supervised model through a single prediction callback. It covers
regression, binary and multiclass classification, and right-censored survival
analysis with time-dependent attributions.

The sampling (permutation) estimator is used: every coalition prediction is
issued in **one batched call**, and the marginal-contribution reduction runs
in parallel C++ via `RcppParallel`. Pairwise interaction values are available.
Alongside the familiar plots, the package ships three opinionated multivariate
views and one colour system with selectable styles.

## Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ielbadisy/shapvalues")
```

## Quick start

```{r quickstart}
library(shapvalues)

fit <- lm(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)
sv  <- shapvalues(fit, X = mtcars[, -1], bg = mtcars[, -1], nsim = 100)
sv
```

Local accuracy holds exactly for the Monte Carlo estimate:

```{r localacc}
max(abs(rowSums(sv$phi) + sv$baseline - sv$prediction[, 1]))
```

## Standard plots

```{r beeswarm}
sv_beeswarm(sv)
```

```{r importance, fig.height = 3.6}
sv_importance(sv)
```

```{r waterfall}
sv_waterfall(sv, row = 1)
```

```{r dependence}
sv_dependence(sv, feature = "wt", colour_by = "hp")
```

## Pairwise interaction values

```{r interaction}
svi <- shapvalues(lm(mpg ~ wt * hp + disp + drat + qsec, data = mtcars),
                  mtcars[, c("wt", "hp", "disp", "drat", "qsec")],
                  mtcars[, c("wt", "hp", "disp", "drat", "qsec")],
                  nsim = 120, interactions = TRUE)
sv_interaction(svi, feature = "wt", interact = "hp")
```

## Survival: SurvSHAP(t)

```{r survival}
library(survival)
cox <- coxph(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno + celltype, data = veteran, x = TRUE)
pf  <- function(object, newdata, times) {
  s <- summary(survfit(object, newdata = newdata), times = times, extend = TRUE)$surv
  t(matrix(s, nrow = length(times)))
}
svs <- shapvalues(cox, veteran[, c("age", "karno", "celltype")],
                  veteran[, c("age", "karno", "celltype")], pred_fun = pf,
                  times = c(30, 90, 180, 270, 365), task = "survival", nsim = 60)
sv_surv(svs, row = 1)
```

## Multivariate attribution views

These summarise the whole attribution vector of each observation rather than
marginalising one feature at a time.

**Compass** — each observation sits where its `|SHAP|` mass points; distance
from the centre is the explanation concentration `EC` in `[0, 1]`.

```{r compass, fig.height = 5.4}
sv_compass(sv)
```

**Fingerprint** — a radial `|SHAP|` signature, here one per k-means cluster of
the SHAP profiles.

```{r fingerprint, fig.height = 3.4}
sv_fingerprint(sv, k = 3)
```

**Pathway** — an alluvial of the top-ranked contributors: node = feature, flow
width = observations, flow colour = the sign of the dominant contribution.

```{r pathway, fig.height = 4.4}
sv_pathway(sv, rank = 3)
```

## One colour system, selectable styles

Every plot draws from `sv_style()`: the package's own diverging pair, or a
`viridisLite` map.

```{r styles, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3, fig.show = "hold", out.width = "50%"}
sv_beeswarm(sv, max_features = 6, title = "style = \"shapvalues\"")
sv_beeswarm(sv, max_features = 6, title = "style = \"plasma\"", style = "plasma")
```

## Benchmark

`shapvalues` is the fastest model-agnostic SHAP estimator on CRAN in the tests
under `inst/benchmarks/` (3-6x faster than `fastshap`, 10-25x faster than
`kernelshap`, at accuracy on par with `fastshap`). Run
`Rscript inst/benchmarks/bench-shapvalues.R` to reproduce.
